packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
Packet 15 - blind image reading (unverified)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading for this packet. Beyond the rules: I cropped, enlarged, rotated and mirrored regions of the packet images with PIL so I could read small notes. I opened no other files.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two faces of one narrow vertical parchment strip, about 4.5-5 cm wide and about 20 cm tall going by the ruler; it looks like a binding strip or guard. The lower end is cut on the diagonal and has a crack.
- Face A (overview image-001; tiles image-002 top, image-003 lower; the tiles overlap only a little around image-002 bottom / image-003 top):
  * At the top is a short note in brown ink in a small cursive/textualis hand (two lines). The second line has a horizontal stroke through it, which may be a deletion or just a long abbreviation stroke.
  * Below it is a line of large display letters in alternating blue and red: "...A . VII ." It is cut at the left edge, so more letters were probably there to the left. It looks like a chapter or quire number, or a running number, in coloured capitals.
  * At the left edge, under the coloured line, are short line-ends of small brown text (5 or 6 lines, then more groups lower down). These are the right-hand ends of lines whose beginnings were trimmed off at the left. They look like short abbreviated references, perhaps a column of marginal allegations or an index, but I can't confirm that.
  * In the middle area are slightly larger notes, apparently in a different hand or campaign: "...terius . c . sidue(?)" and "S . e . eq(?)". Lower down is a block of four short reference-style lines ("S . u(?)ij . c . lectas(?)" etc.).
  * The lower half is blank, ruled and stained. At the bottom is a turned or folded section with a few lines of larger gothic letters running sideways (perpendicular to the strip). They show faintly through, or are offset, and I could not read them.
- Face B (overview image-004; tiles image-005 top, image-006 lower):
  * Most of this face is covered by a later paper lining or repair. A narrow parchment margin shows at the left.
  * At the top, under a brown leather or adhesive band, is one line of small text: "...ẽ(?) . ii . iii . [..]p[..]q(?)[...] ." I could only read part of it.
  * At the bottom, below the paper, on a parchment flap, are two lines of LARGER gothic book hand running sideways: line 1 is partly cut, "...nuod(?) iui." / "...uoid iui."; line 2 is "...ra dñm ie custodi" (it could be "...ra dñm (et?) custodi"). There is a small red mark (a red stroke or rubric fragment) to the right of line 1.

SELECTED SPANS
I read all visible writing; there is very little of it. Unread: the sideways larger script at the bottom of face A (show-through/offset, too faint), and most of the trimmed line-ends at the left edge of face A.

TRANSCRIPTION

Face A

image-002 (top note above the coloured line; lines counted from the top of image-002)
image-002 l.1: ⁻lxxviij(?) q(?) . v .     [first letter reads like "l" with a superscript stroke; "q" could be "d"]
image-002 l.2: admittit(ur)(?) [st...ctes(?)] .     [the second word has a long stroke through it, possibly a deletion; it may read "stricte" or "decres"; uncertain]

image-002 l.3 (coloured capitals): ...[A or Y, blue] . [C or D?, red] . V(blue) I(red) L(blue) .   [as it shows: "A . C(?) . VIL ." The letters are alternately blue and red, and the left edge is trimmed]

image-002 ll.4-7 (left-edge line ends, trimmed at the left; very faint)
image-002 l.4: [illegible] ꝑ(?)[..]e(?) [..]
image-002 l.5: [..] re(?) . ꝑ(?) sen(?)
image-002 l.6: [..]ua(?) ꝑ re(?) ꞇ(?) re[..]
image-002 l.7: [..]ue(?) de(?) .[..]
image-002 l.8: (gap)
image-002 l.9: ꝯ(?) . [..]ue(?) [.] du[..] .

image-002 l.10 (larger note, centre): ...terius(?) . c . sidue(?) .     [the long stroke reaching in from the left may be a line-filler or the end of a deleted word; "sidue" could be "si duo"]
image-002 l.11: S . e . eq(?) .     [a small superscript mark stands above S]

image-002 ll.12-14 (faint left-edge lines)
image-002 l.12: ꝯ(?) p(er)(?)[..] q(?) [..]ue(?) .
image-002 l.13: ꝯ(?) [..]un(?) . e[..] .
image-002 l.14: [..]r . [..] q̄ [..]
image-002 (lower, about 3/4 down): faint traces, perhaps "[..] ꝯ(?) [..]" [illegible]

image-003 (lines counted from the top of image-003)
image-003 l.1-2: faint left-edge traces [illegible]; a stain overlaps them
image-003 l.3: ... c . r(?)ubea(?) .     [could also be "ruben", "ruber" or "tuber"]
image-003 l.4: S . u(?)iij(?) . c . lectas(?) .     [the first word has a superscript mark over S]
image-003 l.5: l . xxi(?) q(?) . i(?) . i(?)s(?)ta(?)c(?) .
image-003 l.6: l(?) . iij(?) . q . vi(?) . h(?)ac(?)re(?) .     [could be "S . iij . q . vi . h(?)..."]
image-003 l.7: J . q(?) [ꝯ?] . e(?)s(?)ro(?)uitas(?) .     [could be "ꝯ . 93(?) ..."; the last word could be "extremitas" or "seueritas"; uncertain]
Below these lines on image-003 there is no further writing until the folded strip at the bottom edge (top of the sideways script just visible).

image-001 bottom (overview only; sideways larger gothic letters on the folded section): about 2 lines. I tried rotating and mirroring the crop but the letters stayed ambiguous; this is probably show-through from face B. [illegible]

Face B

image-005 l.1 (under the leather/adhesive band at the top): [..]ẽ(?) . ii . iii(?) . [..]p[..]q[..]s(?) .     [faint; the band covers part of the line]

image-004 bottom (overview; the image-006 tile cuts off at the top of these lines, so I read them from an enlarged crop of the overview); the lines run sideways, reading upward along the strip:
image-004 bottom l.1: ...[n]uoid(?) iui(?) .     [cut at the top/left; there is a red mark after it]
image-004 bottom l.2: ...ra dñm ie custodi     [dñm = d(omi)n(u)m or d(omi)n(u)m(?); the macron over "ñ" is clear; "ie" could be "&" or "ie"; custodi is clear]

LIMITATIONS
- This is a binding strip, so only marginal notes and a few words of main text survive. The main text (the larger gothic book hand) appears only at the folded bottom on both faces, and only about 2 lines on each.
- The image-006 native tile stops before the bottom script, so my reading there comes from the reduced overview.
- A later paper repair covers most of face B.
- The face A notes are small and faint. The trimmed line ends at the left can't be read reliably.
- Suggested next step: a native-resolution tile of the bottom 5 cm of both faces (the folded flap), and raking light on the left-edge line ends of face A.
